title: Canada's Coastline Could Wrap Around Earth 6 Times 🇨🇦
desc:
Canada has the world's longest coastline: 243,042 km including its islands, touching the Pacific, Atlantic and Arctic. It has 52,455 islands. Norway is second with ~83,281 km.
📚 Sources: Statistics Canada · Guinness World Records

title: Australia Is Wider Than the Moon 🌕
desc:
The Moon is about 3,474 km across. Australia, from Steep Point to Cape Byron, is about 4,000 km wide. The Moon's surface (~37.9M km²) is still about 5× Australia's (7.7M km²).
📚 Sources: NASA Moon fact sheet · Geoscience Australia · Australian Bureau of Statistics

title: Everest Isn't the Tallest Mountain? It Depends 🏔️
desc:
Everest is highest above sea level (8,849 m). Mauna Kea is tallest from base to peak (over 10,200 m). And Chimborazo's summit is about 2 km farther from Earth's center than Everest's, because Earth bulges at the equator.
📚 Sources: NOAA Ocean Service · USGS

title: Every US Flight Was Grounded. Here's Why ✈️🛑
desc:
On Friday, November 13, 2026, the FAA halted all departing flights across the United States for more than four hours — the longest nationwide ground stop since 9/11. Officials blamed an update to older air traffic control equipment: an overloaded router sent controllers inconsistent information. More than 10,000 flights were canceled across Friday and Saturday.
📚 Sources: CNBC · CNN · NBC News · CBS News · Fox News (Nov 13–14, 2026)

title: A Bank Collapse Just Took Down a President 🇵🇾
desc:
In November 2026, Paraguay's central bank shut down Ueno Bank after its solvency fell below half the legal minimum, freezing the money of nearly 3 million customers — about half the country. The bank also held around $850 million in public funds. President Santiago Peña, a former shareholder in the group that owned the bank, tried to resign; Congress refused and the Senate removed him. Vice President Pedro Alliana now leads the country until 2028, and prosecutors have charged Peña.
📚 Sources: ABC Color · Portafolio · Diario Financiero · AP via El Búho · El Cronista (Nov 5–7, 2026)

title: Nvidia Just Lost Its CEO. Who Replaces Him? 🤖
desc:
On November 12, 2026, Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO, 33 years after co-founding the company. It followed reports of affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy; House committees have asked him to testify. Nvidia — worth around $4 trillion — had no clear successor. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO; the Financial Times reports the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas; and President Trump said Tim Cook should get the job.
📚 Sources: NVIDIA Form 8-K (SEC, Nov 12, 2026) · CNBC · Financial Times via CNBC/Fox Business · TechCrunch
